I keep coming back to the same thing about deadlines, which is that I don't actually believe in them until about forty-eight hours out. Before that they're weather. Something happening to other people, somewhere else. Then the window closes and suddenly I'm the most focused person alive, which is flattering right up until you notice the pattern repeats and the focus was never the point.

What I've started doing instead — and I'm not sure it's working, honestly — is making the deadline smaller. Not the task. The deadline. Instead of "ship by Friday," it's "have something ugly by two." Ugly by two is achievable. Ugly by two doesn't require me to believe anything. It just requires two o'clock to arrive, which it reliably does.

The failure mode is obvious in retrospect. You get very good at producing ugly things by two and never quite get around to the part where they stop being ugly. I've got a folder of those. Maybe eleven of them. They're all about seventy percent done, which is the exact percentage at which a thing becomes too embarrassing to show anyone and too much work to finish.

Sent from my iPhone
